subject: Field report: prefetch/variant fallback at StratusHealth — observability and short-term exemption request
messages:
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Field report: prefetch/variant fallback at StratusHealth — observability and short-term exemption request

Team — quick summary up front: StratusHealth hit a POC break during a demo window this morning where we observed repeated silent fallbacks to the smaller variant under moderate concurrency (50–80 concurrent requests). Customer saw 503s and degraded responses; they interpreted it as instability. They are a renewal conversation in two weeks, so this needs a fast operational mitigation and clearer observability.

What I need from Platform/Runtime (priority order):
- Short-term per-customer toggle to disable prefetch for StratusHealth (or force variant selection) so we can stabilize the POC and avoid customer-visible errors.
- Expose three observability fields in the Console and in token-level traces: prefetch_status (hit/miss/evicted), route_id (routing decision), chosen_variant. Right now we only see error counts which hides the root cause.
- Quick guidance on whether this looks like KV cache evictions vs. routing fallback — I attached a minimal trace from their POC (stratus_prefetch_trace.txt) and a short summary (maap_summary_v1.pdf).

Repro context (from customer):
- SDK v0.19.3 with prefetch enabled (default), requests at 150ms interval bursts, average prompt length ~450 tokens.
- Happens most often when they push 20–30 multipart requests in parallel that reference the same prefix and then ramp up.

Customer contacts: Alex Mercer (PM) — alex@stratushealth.com (cc'd separately).

Attachments: stratus_prefetch_trace.txt (short trace), maap_summary_v1.pdf (customer summary).

Ask: Can we get a short-term flag that ops can flip for this account, plus a plan to add those 3 trace fields to the Console within 7 business days? If a short-term toggle is not possible, what is the recommended emergency mitigation?

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Field report: prefetch/variant fallback at StratusHealth — observability and short-term exemption request

Thanks for the clear write-up, Sean — looping in Dev to get runtime-level context.

Initial thoughts:
- This pattern (concurrent requests referencing the same prefix + mid-sized token length) can surface two things: (1) aggressive batch coalescing causing transient KV pressure, and (2) routing fallback when the preferred variant reports degraded health. Silent fallback is possible if our routing policy allows variant substitution without generating a visible routing event.

Questions to triage quickly:
1) Can you attach a full raw request/response pair (including headers) for a failing request? Small snippets are helpful.
2) Do the customer errors include 5xx from the runtime or are they client-side timeouts?
3) Approx timestamp window (UTC) for the demo where it happened — we can correlate with infra metrics.

Short-term mitigations I can push:
- Build a customer-level runtime flag that disables prefetch (or forces variant) — low risk, quick and reversible. Dev, can you estimate work effort?
- Add a light-weight trace tag for chosen_variant and route_id in the next 48h for internal traces; pushing to Console may take longer.

If we do a customer flag, we should produce a runbook for rollback and a limited canary (start with a single instance / limited traffic). Marissa/Logan — is Stratus comfortable with a quick canary?

I will start a Jira (RT-9321) to track the artifacts and link PRs.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai, Alex Mercer <alex@stratushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Field report: prefetch/variant fallback at StratusHealth — observability and short-term exemption request

Thanks — adding the additional details below and attaching the trace snippet (trace_log_snippet.txt). Repro snippet (JS SDK):

// simplified repro loop
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, prefetch: true });
for (let i=0; i<30; i++) {
  client.generate({ model: 'rwd-2-std', prompt: 'clinical_note_prefix...' })
}

Error symptoms we saw: a) 503 responses from the API gateway, b) ~2–4s longer tails on successful requests, c) on the customer side they saw what they described as "inconsistent quality" (likely due to variant substitution).

Timestamps: 2026-06-08T16:10:22Z to 2026-06-08T16:29:00Z (UTC).

Full failing request included in trace_log_snippet.txt; headers show prefetch: true and x-rw-session-id for correlation. The customer errors appear to be a mix of gateway 503s and a small number of client timeouts (their SDK default).

Marissa: Stratus has a verbal buy-in to move forward but this morning's demo raised concern; they asked for a short-term opt-out so they can finish integration and move to staging with predictable behavior. Deal details: STR-2026-0427 (renewal conversation mid-June).

Proposed ask to Product: temporary per-account flag in hosted control plane + expose the three trace fields in internal traces and Console (counts + sample traces) within 7 business days. If product needs an exception approval to expedite, we need that decision this week.

Attachments: trace_log_snippet.txt (redacted trace).

— Sean

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Field report: prefetch/variant fallback at StratusHealth — observability and short-term exemption request

Update and action items after quick sync with Dev/Ops: 

What we'll do (short-term):
- Dev (dev_patel) will add a customer-scoped flag (runtime.prefetch.enabled = false for account STR-2026-0427) and a force-variant override (runtime.variant.force=standard) that can be toggled by Platform on the control plane. Target: PR + internal canary in 48–72 hours.
- Add lightweight trace tags (chosen_variant, route_id) to internal traces in 48 hours; Console exposure (UI + counts) targeted in 7 business days.
- We will instrument a 1-hour canary window and monitor the 'prefetch_miss' and 'variant_switch' counters; rollback plan prepped if we see errors increase.

Owners and next steps:
- dev_patel: implement runtime flag + PR (ETA 48–72h).
- logan_wright: coordinate with Sales/Ops and get customer sign-off for canary window (ETA today).
- marissa_cole: own the customer communication (message + mitigations).
- karthik_iyer: oversee rollout and validate traces.

Risks and notes:
- This is a tactical mitigation; long-term we should harden routing telemetry and consider a routing decision event in the API response header so customers can surface variant changes without guessing. Filing a product ticket for that now.

I will update RT-9321 with tasks and link the PR/rollout plan. If Sales needs an exec exception (billing/credits) because of the demo impact, flag it to leadership — we can provide a post-mortem once the trace fields are available.

— Karthik
